title: A Cheetah Ran 100 Metres in 5.95 Seconds (Bolt Does 9.58)

scenes.text: A cheetah ran 100 metres in 5.95 seconds.
Her name was Sarah. Eleven years old. On a certified track in Ohio, 2012.
Usain Bolt's world record is 9.58 seconds. She beat it by over three and a half seconds.
Her top speed on radar: 61 miles an hour. Each stride, 22 feet.
The trick is her spine. It flexes like a spring, so her back legs reach past her front ones.
5.95 seconds. And she was eleven. An old lady, for a cheetah.

description:
In June 2012, an 11-year-old cheetah named Sarah ran 100 metres in 5.95 seconds from a standing start on a USA Track and Field certified course set up by the Cincinnati Zoo.
Usain Bolt's human world record is 9.58 seconds. Sarah's top speed was radar-timed at 61 miles an hour, and cheetahs cover about 22 feet per stride thanks to a flexible spine that works like a spring.
Who wins a 100 metre race: a cheetah, a greyhound or a racehorse? Comment below.
first_comment: Sarah's own previous record was 6.13 seconds, set when she was eight. She got faster with age. Which animal would you put money on against a cheetah?
